requirements.evidence: All contract items are present: .env.example:1,7-8; phpunit.xml:22-24; config/mail.php:129-134 and the pegafila theme at resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:240-246; routes/web.php:16-31; lang/pt_BR.json:559,804; controllers, request and views as specified. Edge cases are covered: same response for unknown e-mail (PasswordResetLinkController.php:30-32), invalid token (NewPasswordController.php:40-44), and id/hash mismatch (VerifyEmailController.php:18-20).

conventions.evidence: Uses a Form Request for the multi-field reset (NewPasswordRequest.php:26-32) and inline validation for the single-field request (PasswordResetLinkController.php:28); routes use guest/throttle/signed correctly (routes/web.php:16-31); CHANGELOG updated (CHANGELOG.md:26,30). Deviation: the two auth views duplicate the full page shell and field markup (resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-21 and reset-password.blade.php:1-21) instead of extracting an anonymous Blade component.

security.evidence: Server-side validation on both inputs (PasswordResetLinkController.php:28; NewPasswordRequest.php:28-32); uniform anti-enumeration response (PasswordResetLinkController.php:30-32); verification authorization via EmailVerificationRequest (VerifyEmailController.php:18) plus auth/signed/throttle (routes/web.php:29-31); all output is escaped with {{ }} and there is no {!! !!} in either view (forgot-password.blade.php:39; reset-password.blade.php:26,36).

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Auth/PasswordResetTest.php:14-164 covers the form, guest-only access, known/unknown e-mail, invalid e-mail, throttling, token/e-mail binding, successful reset (password, remember_token, PasswordReset event, redirect/status), invalid token, confirmation and weak passwords; tests/Feature/Auth/VerifyEmailTest.php:18-57 covers signed link, hash mismatch, id mismatch and unsigned link; tests/Feature/Mail/AccountEmailsTest.php:11-56 covers the pt-BR subjects/body/subcopy, PegaFila name, pegafila theme and inlined brand color.

simplicity.evidence: Controllers are small and reuse Laravel's Password broker and framework notifications (NewPasswordController.php:28-38; PasswordResetLinkController.php:30-32). The avoidable duplication is the copied auth page shell and field markup in resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-21 and reset-password.blade.php:1-21.

readability.evidence: Clear names and small focused methods with docblocks (PasswordResetLinkController.php:12-33; NewPasswordController.php:12-47; VerifyEmailController.php:11-24); Pest tests are consistently named and structured; no dead code, debugging output or unused imports.

scope.evidence: The diff touches only task-related files: .env.example, phpunit.xml, config/mail.php, the pegafila theme CSS, routes/web.php, the two password-reset controllers plus request, the two auth views, lang/pt_BR.json, three test files and CHANGELOG.md. No login/registration, Livewire, SCSS/JS, nginx/Docker or other out-of-scope changes.

issues.explanation: Both auth views repeat the same full-page shell (head, Vite/CDN block, Bulma section/columns/box) instead of extracting an anonymous Blade component, contrary to the project's Blade-components convention.
Only CHANGELOG.md is updated; the README/docs listed by the docs-freshness convention were not touched, so the docs-sync checklist is only partly satisfied.

review.summary: The change implements the requested pt-BR account e-mails, pegafila mail theme, password-reset flow and signed verification route, with a broad Pest suite covering the main failure and authorization paths. It is approvable with nits: the two auth views duplicate their full page shell instead of using an anonymous Blade component, and documentation beyond the changelog was not updated.
